tasks.short: Develop nursing service goals, priorities, policies and procedures

steps.what: Determine nursing service philosophy, goals and policy requirements with stakeholders
Draft nursing service policies and procedures from the agreed brief

loop.purpose: Turn an agreed service brief into policy prose
loop.input: Chosen goals, priorities, source passages, scope and unresolved questions
loop.output: Draft policy with source links and explicit unresolved clauses
loop.check: Specialist checks intended priorities, responsibilities, conditions, clinical meaning and omissions against the brief and sources; unsupported clauses are rejected
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved clauses are written manually or referred back to stakeholders
loop.why_not_simpler: Native structures remove formatting work first; expressing different stakeholder requirements still involves language judgement

steps.what: Reconcile feedback and finalise policy proposal for formal governance

tasks.design: Use a native policy structure in {DOCS}, then draft prose only from the specialist's agreed brief and selected sources. The specialist reconciles feedback and verifies the exact proposal; adoption remains a separate formal governance decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy composition takes time, but service priorities cannot be inferred from old documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded language drafting can support expression of decisions already made by people.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing priorities, resolving conflicting responsibilities and judging clinical implications.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible priorities and build commitment to the proposed service direction.
tasks.altitude: Less prose composition; no new right to adopt policy or set clinical authority.

reach.task: Contribute a practical requirement to a policy review
reach.learn: Service governance and evidence-based policy writing

evidence.claim: Drafting policy prose from an agreed brief is plausible; choosing service priorities and validating clinical meaning remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary ends with a verified proposal, not policy adoption or implementation. The separate specialty standards task overlaps this work and cannot yield additive savings for the same policy.

The specialist produces scope, goals, priorities, responsibilities, exact source passages and unresolved questions in s1, including capture and appraisal time. Missing requirements return to stakeholder discussion or manual drafting.
Native templates and version control are tested before model use. No model decides goals, invents requirements or publishes a policy.
Final proposal review and release are fully counted in s3. Formal governance review outside this boundary is unchanged; it is not silently transferred from the specialist.
The composition share and reduction are E1 scenarios requiring observed validation.
unknowns: Existing policy structures, proposal composition time and formal governance route
research_questions: Does assisted drafting preserve agreed responsibilities and clinical conditions after full review?

already_counted.description: Stakeholder judgement and final proposal review remain.

incremental.description: Specialist audits source fidelity and updates brief-to-draft controls.
Document owner maintains access and validates tool changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact policy proposal, agreed brief, source versions and resolved feedback; any change voids proposal release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=87.5, gross=12.5 less three focal upkeep hours gives net=9.5. High assumes composition halves; low assumes extensive reconciliation leaves only upkeep-equivalent gains. Priority setting and final review remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead nursing regulatory and accreditation implementation

steps.what: Interpret regulatory or accreditation requirements and assign nursing implementation actions
Track accreditation implementation actions and follow up missing evidence
Lead nursing implementation and resolve compliance gaps with responsible staff

tasks.design: Configure native action owners, due dates and evidence links in {PROJECT}, linked to requirements in {DOCS}. The specialist still interprets requirements, checks submitted evidence and leads corrective work; an updated status never certifies compliance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated status chasing can obscure the substantive compliance gap.
tasks.enabler_now: Native work registers can consolidate progress and reminder views without automated regulatory judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether practice actually meets a requirement and changing behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge weak evidence and obtain workable corrective action.
tasks.altitude: Less status collation; implementation and compliance responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain evidence for a local corrective action
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency and traceability to requirements

evidence.claim: A native action register can reduce repeated status collation, while requirements interpretation and evidence sufficiency remain human judgement.

assumptions: Boundary covers specialist leadership and tracking; action owners' actual corrective work and a regulator's assessment are outside and unchanged. No external filing or certification is automated.

The specialist captures requirement identifier and version, owner, action, due date and evidence expectation in s1. Owners produce dated status and evidence links during existing follow-up work; two additional other-role hours allow any extra structured update burden.
Retained s2 time includes checking updates, evidence meaning and manual follow-up. Missing or unreliable fields remain unknown and use manual contact, never an automatic completed status.
Test native work-register views and reminders before custom automation; no model loop is needed for status organisation.
Twenty percent status tracking is an E1 scenario to validate.
unknowns: Applicable national requirements, owner update burden and existing register functions
research_questions: Does native tracking save specialist time after counting evidence checks and additional owner capture?

already_counted.description: Requirement interpretation and implementation leadership remain.
Status checks and missing-evidence follow-up remain.

incremental.description: Specialist checks register controls and overdue-status quality.
Action owners supply any additional structured progress entries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 less two focal upkeep hours gives net=8. High assumes status tracking halves; low assumes incomplete updates require enough manual chasing to leave only upkeep-equivalent gains. Corrective work and interpretation keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Give clients information for informed health and treatment decisions

steps.what: Select applicable information for the client's health care decision
Present treatment information and check understanding and unanswered questions

tasks.design: Use vetted patient material in {DOCS} with relevant care context from the {OTHER} clinical record. The specialist selects what applies, explains options and checks understanding; supplying a leaflet alone does not complete informed discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clients need information related to their own choices and concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted education sources are available, but they do not establish patient understanding.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining uncertainty and balancing information with the client's preferences and capacity.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, invite questions and explain without steering the person's choice.
tasks.altitude: No change in decision rights or time for informed discussion.

reach.task: Improve access to understandable decision information

evidence.claim: Thuisarts provides guideline-based vetted patient education, as described in the digest.
Choosing applicable information and checking understanding remain contextual human work.

assumptions: Boundary covers specialist preparation and explanation, not deciding treatment on behalf of the client or a separate consent-recording task.

Treating professionals produce the offered care options through existing care planning, unchanged outside this boundary. The specialist checks applicability in s1; client preferences and questions are elicited during s2, with all contact time retained.
No structured preference profile or generated personalised advice is assumed. Missing information is clarified with the responsible clinician and client.
Review native patient-information access first; no new application, translation model or automatic advice is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because existing material selection and discussion are unchanged.
unknowns: Approved patient information and available language or accessibility support
research_questions: Which explanation barriers persist despite current vetted materials?

already_counted.description: Selection, explanation and understanding checks remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Both straightforward explanations and clients needing additional support retain selection and discussion time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review department or committee issues and set the decision agenda
Chair nursing committee discussion and establish decisions and responsibilities

tasks.design: Retain agenda judgement and chairing with the specialist, using existing {DOCS} committee papers. Routine scheduling or minutes are separate work when actually present; this design does not invent them as removable chairing time.
tasks.previous_blocker: A chair must manage conflicting views and work within the committee's remit.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital papers can support access but do not replace facilitation or decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Ensuring dissent is heard and decisions have accountable owners.
tasks.human_edge: Keep discussion fair, recognise unresolved risk and establish a clear outcome.
tasks.altitude: Chairing responsibilities and committee authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Facilitate a focused nursing improvement discussion
reach.learn: Meeting remit, fair facilitation and decision clarity

evidence.claim: Chairing involves prioritisation, facilitation and accountable decisions that document access does not remove.

assumptions: Boundary is the chair's substantive preparation and facilitation, not secretariat scheduling or minutes. Members' participation is unchanged outside the focal baseline.
Members produce submissions as existing committee work; chair review and agenda creation remain fully counted in s1. No structured decision-ready agenda is presumed to arrive free.
Incomplete papers require direct clarification within retained preparation; no model decides priorities or records a decision as approved.
Test native document access and committee tools before future additions; no change is proposed now.
Zero incremental upkeep because there is no new process. Specific policy discussions overlapping other tasks must be allocated once.
unknowns: Committee remit and separate secretariat responsibilities
research_questions: Which recurring chairing burden is clerical rather than substantive facilitation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine committees and contentious decisions both retain substantive preparation and facilitation; no secretariat saving enters the chair's denominator.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Policy composition and compliance tracking receive limited support while service priorities, implementation leadership and patient explanation stay human.
reach: Coach nurses on evidence for corrective actions
Help patient representatives improve understandable information
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with clearer proposals and visible implementation gaps who remains responsible for judgement, patient communication and governance.
